title: Reverse Words in a String III

analysis.problem_summary: Reverse the characters of each word in a space-delimited sentence while preserving space characters and word order.
analysis.intuition: Since words are separated by spaces and stay in their original relative positions, we can process each word independently. Converting the string into a mutable character array allows us to locate each word's start and end boundaries using two pointers, then reverse the characters in that specific sub-range in-place before constructing the final string.
approach: Convert the input string `s` into a character array `charArr` and initialize both `start` and `end` pointers to index `0`.
Iterate through `charArr` with a outer `while` loop that runs as long as `start` is within array bounds.
Advance `end` using an inner `while` loop until it encounters a space character `' '` or reaches the end of the array, defining the current word boundary.
Call the `reverse` helper method to swap characters in `charArr` from index `start` to `end - 1` using a two-pointer approach that moves inward.
Advance both `start` and `end` to `end + 1` to skip the space character and position the pointers at the beginning of the next word.
Construct and return a new `String` from the modified `charArr` after all words have been reversed.
analysis.why_it_works: By using `end` to find the delimiting space, the interval `[start, end - 1]` strictly bounds a single word. Applying a standard two-pointer character reversal on this precise sub-array guarantees that each character within the word is mirrored around its midpoint, reversing the word while leaving spaces and the order of surrounding words unchanged.
analysis.time_explanation: Each character in the string is visited a constant number of times—once to locate word boundaries and at most once during the character reversal process.
analysis.space_explanation: Creating the character array `charArr` and the resulting string requires auxiliary memory proportional to the length of the string `s`.
analysis.key_takeaway: To reverse segments of a string separated by a delimiter, use dynamic pointer bounds to isolate each segment and apply localized two-pointer reversals.
